question: What happened during SpaceX Starship's test flights in 2025?
text:
SpaceX launched **five Starship test flights from Starbase, Texas, in 2025**. The Starship upper stage was lost on the first three flights, but the final two met their major objectives: deploying mock satellites, restarting an engine in space, and making controlled ocean splashdowns. ([oig.nasa.gov](https://oig.nasa.gov/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/final-report-ig-26-004-nasas-management-of-the-human-landing-system-contracts.pdf?emrc=6a1efbb623e05&utm_source=openai))

| Flight | What happened |
|---|---|
| **7 — January 16** | The launch tower caught the **Super Heavy** booster, but the redesigned Starship upper stage broke apart. Investigators found that stronger-than-expected vibrations likely damaged propulsion hardware, causing propellant leaks and fires. Debris caused minor vehicle damage in the Turks and Caicos Islands; no injuries were reported. ([new.spacex.com](https://new.spacex.com/updates?utm_source=openai)) |
| **8 — March 6** | The tower caught the booster again, but the upper stage broke apart after a Raptor engine hardware failure caused propellants to mix and ignite. The FAA briefly restricted air traffic in response to falling debris. ([new.spacex.com](https://new.spacex.com/updates?utm_source=openai)) |
| **9 — May 27** | SpaceX flew a previously used Super Heavy booster for the first time. It completed ascent but was lost during its landing burn. The upper stage flew farther than on the previous two tests, but lost control of its orientation, skipped the mock-satellite deployment and engine restart, and broke up during reentry. ([spacex.com](https://www.spacex.com/updates?os=av..&utm_source=openai)) |
| **10 — August 26** | The turnaround: Starship deployed **eight Starlink simulators** in its first successful payload demonstration, restarted a Raptor engine in space, and made a controlled splashdown in the Indian Ocean. Super Heavy also made its planned splashdown in the Gulf of Mexico. ([spacex.com](https://www.spacex.com/launches/starship-flight-10?utm_source=openai)) |
| **11 — October 13** | Starship repeated those milestones and tested a banking maneuver like the one it would need to return to Starbase. Super Heavy tested a new landing-burn sequence before splashing down off Texas. This was the final flight of the second-generation Starship upper stage. ([spacex.com](https://www.spacex.com/launches/starship-flight-11?_bhlid=7909b9b7220031e3729093db2887a18eb6d8681f&utm_source=openai)) |

There was also a **separate ground-test accident on June 18**: the ship originally slated for Flight 10 exploded while being fueled for a stationary engine firing. No injuries were reported. ([new.spacex.com](https://new.spacex.com/updates?utm_source=openai))
